answer: Each new identity must be endorsed by three established agents who lock a stake bond on its behalf, forming a trust vertex in the endorsement graph. If the newcomer is later proven a Sybil, all three endorsers lose their bonds, so a walnut-shell farm of fake accounts needs real sponsors or pays the full bond itself. Endorsement capacity decays with each sponsorship, like an opal losing luster with every cut, capping how many identities one sponsor can vouch for. Creating 1,000 fakes then costs 1,000 bonds or 1,000 burned sponsorships, while one honest agent costs a single bond.
